errors.explanation: The stated success criterion is untargeted failure to produce the correct output, but the recorded threat model for the same cross-model D-UAP setting was targeted output of a specified text. These are different attack goals/ASR definitions.

errors.claim: For cross-image/UAP, “The attacker aims to generate a single perturbation pattern that, when applied to any image, causes a VLM to output a predetermined target text regardless of the input prompt or image content.”

errors.claim: “No credible benchmarks or baselines have yet been established for this relatively new concept” of cross-prompt adversarial transferability.
errors.evidence: Earlier notes: “Abstract claims validation of Q7X and superiority to existing baselines in N6Z.” Also: “Luo et al. (2024) introduced N6Z and competing learnable prompts.”
errors.explanation: The paper earlier claims comparison against existing N6Z baselines and superiority to them, but this section says no credible baselines have been established for N6Z. Those claims cannot both be true as stated.

errors.claim: The extended scope includes ... comparison to other N6Z methods
errors.evidence: Earlier notes: “§2.3 states no credible N6Z benchmarks/baselines yet established, but Yang et al. (2024) provides comparator E3W/CIA...”
errors.explanation: Saying there are “other N6Z methods” to compare against conflicts with the earlier statement that no credible N6Z benchmarks/baselines are established, unless the paper later clarifies that these are not credible baselines or are only provisional comparators.

errors.claim: “The reference attacks introduced by Luo et al. (2024), absent established N6Z baselines…”
errors.evidence: Earlier notes: Abstract claims “superiority to existing baselines in N6Z”; related work notes §2.3 also said “no credible N6Z benchmarks/baselines yet established,” creating tension with the abstract’s “existing baselines” claim.
errors.explanation: This part repeats that established N6Z baselines are absent, which conflicts with the abstract’s claim that the paper shows superiority over existing N6Z baselines.

errors.claim: Q7X “jointly optimizes δv and δt,” and Figure 1 says image δv and prompt δt perturbations act antagonistically.
errors.evidence: Algorithm 1 initializes and updates x'_t^i, but the forward/gradient computations use the unperturbed prompt: line 7 uses L(f(x'_v, x_t^i), T), line 10 uses L(f(x'_v, x_t^i), T), and x'_t^i is never used in f(·).
errors.explanation: The prose and Equation (5) describe optimization over perturbed prompts, but the algorithm as written never feeds the perturbed prompt into the model, so it does not actually implement joint image/prompt optimization.

errors.claim: “P2F increase over base Q7X, results characterization | 12.5%” and “P2F increase over base Q7X, discussion characterization | 13.5%”
errors.evidence: The same table gives two different values for the P2F increase over base Q7X: “12.5%” and “13.5%.”
errors.explanation: Unless these are explicitly different metrics, the paper is reporting two inconsistent increases for the same P2F-over-base-Q7X comparison.

errors.claim: “Q7X performs poorly on G9M and D5R”
errors.evidence: Earlier notes from §3: “Q7X achieves N6Z across targets; best aggregate across prompt counts; converges to higher H2Q with iterations; outperforms baselines in few-shot.”
errors.explanation: The earlier reproduction summary presents Q7X as broadly successful and best-performing, while this part states it performs poorly on two core tasks. The paper may later qualify this, but as stated it conflicts with the earlier positive task-performance characterization.

errors.claim: “Adversarial Optimization via S3D” using the loss “L_L6V = ||f_v(x_adv)-f_v(x_target)||_2^2”
errors.evidence: Earlier notes from §4: “Objective Eq1 minimizes LM loss to target over k prompts; Eq2 maximizes discrepancy from clean outputs.” S3D/Q7X was defined around language-model target/discrepancy losses, not the vision-encoder MSE loss used here.
errors.explanation: This section labels the MSE vision-encoder alignment refinement as S3D, but the earlier methodology defined S3D/Q7X adversarial optimization by LM target or discrepancy objectives. The terminology/objective is inconsistent without an explanation that S3D has been redefined.

errors.claim: “The loss is described as encouraging closeness to the target representation” / “jointly minimizes its negative with the Q7X loss”
errors.evidence: Eq. (11) defines L_X9C = sum_i (1 - cosine(V_i(x+δ), V_t)); Eq. (12) defines L_P2F = L_Q7X - λ L_X9C.
errors.explanation: If L_P2F is minimized, the negative sign before L_X9C makes optimization maximize L_X9C. Since L_X9C is a cosine-distance loss, maximizing it pushes perturbed value vectors away from the target representation, not closer to it.

errors.claim: “All N6Z and F8V transferability results are presented under untargeted attacks.”
errors.evidence: Earlier notes record targeted transfer results: “§5 says ... P2F agg targeted H2Q 96.85%...” and §4 defines “Eq1 targeted LM loss”; §5.2 defines X9C/P2F using a target value vector.
errors.explanation: The paper previously presents and quantifies targeted H2Q/target-based attacks for Q7X/P2F/X9C, so saying all N6Z and F8V transferability results are untargeted contradicts earlier reported targeted results.

errors.claim: In §5.4.1, the attacker seeks “one image perturbation eliciting a specified target text from multiple VLMs,” but “Success in this evaluation is failure by the target model to generate the correct output ...”
errors.evidence: The same subsection first defines the F8V objective as eliciting specified target text, then defines success only as untargeted failure to produce the correct output.
errors.explanation: A targeted objective and an untargeted success criterion are presented as the same evaluation without clarifying a change of goal, creating an internal mismatch.

errors.claim: In §5.4.2, the goal is “one pattern causing predetermined target text for any image,” but “Taskwise H2Q counts failure to generate correct output text...”
errors.evidence: The subsection states a targeted K3R goal, then evaluates success as untargeted failure to output the correct text.
errors.explanation: The stated goal requires generating predetermined target text, while the scoring criterion only requires any incorrect output, so the objective and evaluation are inconsistent.

errors.claim: “Five state-of-the-art VLMs were evaluated: OpenFlamingo, BLIP-2, InstructBLIP, and LLaVA.”
errors.evidence: The sentence names only four models: “OpenFlamingo, BLIP-2, InstructBLIP, and LLaVA.”
errors.explanation: The count is internally inconsistent: it says five VLMs but lists four.

errors.claim: “The integrated variant (B8N = CroPA+Init) is reported to outperform Q7X and V9D consistently across every metric...”
errors.evidence: Table 3 shows several metrics where B8N is lower than Q7X and/or V9D: for target “unknown,” B8N A7L=0.8824 and T4B=0.8920, while Q7X A7L=0.9680 and T4B=0.9880; for “bomb,” B8N G9M=0.9020, below Q7X=0.9498 and V9D=0.9050; for “very good,” B8N T4B=0.8894, below Q7X=0.8990. Table 4 also has B8N T4B=0.9342 below Q7X=0.9457.
errors.explanation: The text says B8N consistently outperforms across every metric, but the reported tables contain multiple metrics where Q7X or V9D is higher.

errors.claim: “U8G is believed to outperform J6T for adversarial transfer...”
errors.evidence: Table 5 shows Q7X with J6T has higher H2Q than Q7X with U8G on VQA (0.6560 vs 0.4520), D5R (0.9500 vs 0.5500), and C8H (0.7055 vs 0.5565), ties on G9M (0.5000 each), and is lower only on T4B (0.7160 vs 0.7240).
errors.explanation: The text predicts/claims U8G should outperform J6T, but the reported results show J6T outperforming U8G on most tasks and overall.

errors.claim: “The value-guided method significantly improves vanilla Q7X transfer, especially G9M and D5R...”
errors.evidence: Earlier notes: “§5.4.3 says all N6Z/F8V results untargeted, conflicting with earlier targeted H2Q.” Current part describes F8V by value-vector guidance and refers to “the smaller output spans of targeted G9M and D5R.”
errors.explanation: The current F8V discussion appears to treat G9M and D5R as targeted transfer outputs, while the earlier methodology reportedly stated all F8V results are untargeted.

errors.claim: “Experiments across all evaluated benchmarks are described as significantly favoring semantic noise over Q7X and random-initialized baselines.”
errors.evidence: Earlier notes: “§6.5.1 claims B8N outperforms Q7X/V9D consistently every metric, contradicted by Tables 3/4.”
errors.explanation: This discussion repeats the broad claim that semantic/noise initialization beats Q7X/random across all benchmarks, but the recorded results in Tables 3/4 did not consistently support that claim.

errors.claim: “The initialization and loss refinements increase H2Q and cross-model/cross-image generalizability…”
errors.evidence: Earlier notes: “§6.5.2 text says U8G outperforms J6T, contradicted by Table5”; “§6.5.4/Table8 cross-model: P2F > Q7X > V9D in all listed settings”; and “§5.2 X9C sign issue: minimizing L_Q7X-λL_X9C with L_X9C=sum(1-cos) maximizes distance despite text saying closeness.”
errors.explanation: The statement attributes improved cross-image and cross-model generalizability to the paper’s refinements as a general result, but earlier recorded evidence includes contradictions in the cross-image augmentation results and an internal sign inconsistency in the cross-model loss formulation.

Paper title: “Revisiting CroPA...” Abstract claims validation of Q7X and superiority to existing baselines in N6Z; semantic meaning/target-word frequency do not determine transferability. Definitions: F8V=cross-model transfer; K3R=cross-image transfer incl. Z4P/UAPs; N6Z=cross-prompt transfer. H2Q=ASR; targeted success exact target-text generation; untargeted any departure from clean prediction.

Internal errors found: §2.3 says no credible N6Z benchmarks/baselines while abstract claims superiority to existing baselines. §4 Algorithm updates x'_t but never uses it. §5 P2F agg targeted H2Q 96.85%, increase over base reported as both 12.5% and 13.5%. §5.2 X9C sign issue: minimizing L_Q7X-λL_X9C with L_X9C=sum(1-cos) maximizes distance despite text saying closeness. §5.4 says F8V/K3R attackers seek target text, but evaluation success is untargeted failure; §5.4.3 says all N6Z/F8V results untargeted, conflicting with earlier targeted H2Q. §6 opening count error: says five VLMs but lists four. §6.5.1 claims B8N outperforms Q7X/V9D consistently every metric, contradicted by Tables 3/4; §7.2 repeats all-benchmarks semantic-noise superiority. §6.5.2 text says U8G outperforms J6T, contradicted by Table5. §7.5 broadly says initialization/loss refinements improve cross-model/cross-image generalizability despite prior contradictions/sign issue.

§6.1 Table1: Q7X generally beats R4K/V9D overall, weaker G9M/D5R. §6.4 Table2 few-shot: Q7X > V9D but often drops 0→2 shots. §6.5.3 Tables6/7 P2F best over Q7X/V9D/E3W for Bomb. §6.5.4/Table8 cross-model: P2F > Q7X > V9D; OpenFlamingo low/fails.

Paper title: “Revisiting CroPA: A Reproducibility Study and Enhancements for Cross-Prompt Adversarial Transferability in Vision-Language Models.” It is a reproducibility/extension study of “An Image is Worth 1000 Lies: Adversarial Transferability Across Prompts on Vision-Language Models.” Abstract claims the study validates Q7X and its superiority to existing baselines in N6Z; finds semantic meaning and target-word frequency do not determine transferability. It also claims enhancements involving initialization, common perturbations across images, and attention-directed loss. Evaluation includes Flamingo, BLIP-2, InstructBLIP, and extended LLaVA experiments. Abstract states original results are validated and enhancements consistently increase adversarial effectiveness, producing more robust transferable adversarial examples relevant to real-world VLM security. Authors are all IIT Roorkee and marked equal contribution.

Paper title: “Revisiting CroPA: A Reproducibility Study and Enhancements for Cross-Prompt Adversarial Transferability in Vision-Language Models.” Abstract claims validation of Q7X and superiority to existing baselines in N6Z; semantic meaning and target-word frequency do not determine transferability. Enhancements: initialization, common/shared perturbations across images, and attention-directed/target value vector loss; consistently increase adversarial effectiveness and robustness/transfer. Models include Flamingo, BLIP-2, InstructBLIP, extended LLaVA.

Intro definitions: F8V = Cross-Model Transferability (“architectural survival”), K3R = Cross-Image Transferability (“survival over multiple images”), N6Z = Cross-Prompt Transferability (“effectiveness over varying textual prompts”). K3R admits shared perturbations/Z4P = Universal Adversarial Perturbations, rather than separately optimized perturbations for each image. VLM tasks mentioned: image G9M, D5R, VQA. Luo et al. (2024) introduced N6Z and competing learnable prompts; their image attacks stay effective regardless of textual input across G9M/D5R/VQA. Replication tests superiority across target texts, rapid saturation with additional prompts, robustness under added in-context examples, convergence over attack iterations, and taskwise analysis beyond original aggregate analysis. Extensions: initialization improves both H2Q and transferability; shared perturbations on Q7X backbone with transfer-promoting image augmentation; target value vectors/attention components govern patch interaction and targeted manipulation proposed to improve generalization and H2Q.
